6. This Criminal Revision Application has been filed on behalf of the petitioner challenging the judgment dated 27.07.2023 passed by Sri Vishwa Nath Shukla, learned Sessions Judge, Chaibasa in Cr. Appeal No.42 of 2023 by which the appeal filed on behalf of the petitioner has been dismissed thereby affirming the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 25.04.2023 passed by Sri Binod Kumar, learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Singhbhum West at Chaibasa, in connection with Majhgaon P.S. Case No.22 of 2020 (G.R. Case No.577 of 2020) by which the petitioner has been convicted for the offence under Section 279, 304-A of the IPC and under Section 184 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 and sentenced to undergo R.I. for six months and to pay fine of Rs.1000/ for the offence under Section 279 of IPC, R.I. for two years and to pay fine of Rs.10,000/-
for the offence under Section 304-A of IPC and R.I. for three months and to pay fine of Rs.500/- for the offence under section 184 of Motor Vehicle Act.
sentences._hearing_file: Aziz Ansari vs The State Of Jharkhand on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: 7. I.A. No.876 of 2025 has been filed on behalf of the petitioner under section 438 (1) of BNSS, 2023 for suspension of sentence and for grant of bail to the petitioner, during pendency of the present Criminal Revision Application.
sentences._hearing_file: Aziz Ansari vs The State Of Jharkhand on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text:
8. Heard Mr. Suraj Singh, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. P.K. Chatterjee, learned Spl.PP for the State.
9.
sentences._hearing_file: Aziz Ansari vs The State Of Jharkhand on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the impugned judgments and sentence passed by the learned Courts below are illegal, arbitrary and not sustainable in the eye of law.
sentences._hearing_file: Aziz Ansari vs The State Of Jharkhand on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is submitted that the learned Courts below has wrongly convicted the petitioner for the offence under section 304-A of the IPC.
sentences._hearing_file: Aziz Ansari vs The State Of Jharkhand on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is submitted that the petitioner is in custody since 13.01.2025 and hence, the petitioner may be enlarged on bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Aziz Ansari vs The State Of Jharkhand on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: 10. On the other hand, learned Spl.PP has opposed the prayer for bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Aziz Ansari vs The State Of Jharkhand on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is submitted that due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the vehicle (i.e. the petitioner) the accident taken place and due to which the deceased lady succumb to her injuries and hence, the prayer for bail may be rejected.
sentences._hearing_file: Aziz Ansari vs The State Of Jharkhand on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text:
11. Considering the custody of the petitioner and on the facts and in the circumstances of this case,
the petitioner namely, Aziz Ansari is directed to be released on bail provisionally for a period of six months from today, on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.10,000/- (Ten thousand only) with two sureties of the like amount each, to the satisfaction of Sri Binod Kumar, learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Singhbhum West at Chaibasa/ or his Successor Court in connection with Majhgaon P.S.
Case No.22 of 2020 (G.R. Case No.577 of 2020), subject to payment of Rs.50,000/ to the O.P. No.2 at the time of furnishing bail bonds by way of victim compensation under Section 357-A of the Cr.P.C for the present and one of the bailors must be the own relative of the petitioner.
12.
